title: Local Storage and AsyncStorage
description: Learn how to store data locally on a device using AsyncStorage in React Native to persist user preferences, app state, and offline data.

lessons.title: What is AsyncStorage?
lessons.content: AsyncStorage is an asynchronous, unencrypted, persistent, key-value storage system for React Native apps. It lets you store small amounts of data locally on the device.

lessons.title: Installing AsyncStorage
lessons.content:
AsyncStorage used to be part of React Native core but now is a separate package. Install it using:

```bash
npm install @react-native-async-storage/async-storage
```

Then import it:

```js
import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';
```

Reading Data with AsyncStorage
Removing Data with AsyncStorage
Storing Complex Data Types
lessons.content: AsyncStorage stores only strings. To save objects or arrays, convert them to JSON strings using `JSON.stringify()` before saving, and parse them back with `JSON.parse()` when reading.

lessons.title: Example: Save and Load a User Object
Using AsyncStorage in React Components
Limitations of AsyncStorage
lessons.content:
- Not suitable for large data
- Data stored as plain text (not encrypted)
- Limited to simple key-value pairs
- AsyncStorage operations are asynchronous, so handle accordingly

For complex or secure storage, consider databases like Realm or encrypted storage libraries.

lessons.title: Summary and Best Practices
lessons.content:
- Use AsyncStorage for simple persistent data like settings or user tokens
- Always handle errors in async operations
- Convert objects to JSON strings for storage
- Avoid blocking UI while reading/writing
- Consider user privacy and data security when storing sensitive info
